I've never tried to throw up, fast, or use laxatives afterward to make up for it, though; instead, I just sit there feeling incredibly heavy and ashamed of myself.\n\nDoctor: Do these night eating episodes happen at least once a week for the past 3 months, or have they been going on for a shorter time?\n\nPatient: Yes, it is rare for a week to go by without it happening at least once, and sometimes it's two or three times on the harder weeks. This entire pattern has actually been going on steadily for over a year now, ever since my mother passed away about fourteen months ago.\n\nDoctor: Do these eating episodes happen while you are fully awake and aware, or do they ever occur when you are half-asleep or wake up later with little memory of eating?\n\nPatient: I am definitely fully awake and aware, and it is absolutely not sleep-eating. It usually starts around nine in the evening when I wander into the kitchen to bake or pick at leftovers, and I'm conscious the whole time, even hearing a voice in my head telling me to stop. I remember everything clearly afterward as I sit in the quiet kitchen feeling deep shame.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had periods of eating a large amount of food followed by behaviors like self-induced vomiting, laxative use, fasting, or excessive exercise to prevent weight gain?\n\nPatient: No, I have never done anything like throwing up, using laxatives, or exercising excessively to prevent weight gain. Instead, I just sit there with the intense guilt and shame afterward, which has unfortunately caused me to put on weight and lose my hiking stamina. I don't do anything to try to reverse it.\n\nDoctor: Do you find that most of your food intake happens after dinner or at night, and do you ever wake up from sleep to eat with little or no memory of it afterward?\n\nPatient: Yes, these episodes almost always happen late in the evening after dinner, before I go to bed. However, I never wake up from my sleep to eat, and I don't have any memory loss about it. I am completely awake and vividly remember everything afterward, which is why I feel so much guilt and shame.\n\nDoctor: When you eat at night, are you fully awake and aware the whole time, or do you ever wake up from sleep and find that you ate with little or no memory of it afterward?\n\nPatient: Yes, I am completely awake and aware the entire time. It always happens in the evening before I go to bed, around nine o'clock, and never while I am asleep. I remember everything vividly, which is why I feel so much guilt and shame afterward while sitting in the kitchen looking at the empty dishes.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever wake up from sleep and eat with little or no memory of it afterward, or are these episodes always while you are fully awake and aware?\n\nPatient: No, I never wake up from sleep to eat, and I don't have any memory gaps. These episodes always happen when I am fully awake and aware, usually around nine in the evening before I've even gone to bed. Unfortunately, I remember every single detail, which just leaves me feeling deeply ashamed and full of regret afterward.\n\nDoctor: Do you usually eat most of your daily food after dinner or at night, with little appetite in the morning, or are the episodes mainly discrete binges that can happen at any time of day?\n\nPatient: These are discrete episodes that happen late in the evening, usually around nine o'clock, rather than continuous grazing. I eat a normal supper beforehand and feel comfortably full, but then later I have these sudden, rapid episodes where I eat a huge amount of food in about an hour at the kitchen counter.\n\nDoctor: Do you also regularly wake up during the night to eat, or is the eating only happening in discrete binge episodes while you are fully awake in the evening?\n\nPatient: It only happens while I am fully awake in the evening, usually starting around nine o'clock or in the hour before I go to bed. I never wake up from my sleep during the night to eat.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel a strong urge or need to eat after waking up from sleep during the night, or is the eating only happening as discrete binge episodes while you are fully awake in the evening?\n\nPatient: No, I never wake up during the night with an urge to eat. It only happens as those discrete episodes in the evening when I am fully awake, usually around nine o'clock or in the hour before I go to bed.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least 3 months where most of your daily food intake happened after your evening meal or after waking from sleep, with little or no appetite in the morning?\n\nPatient: While I do eat a large amount of food late in the evening before going to bed, I definitely don't wake up from sleep to eat. I also don't recall having a loss of appetite in the morning.\n\nDoctor: Do you usually have little or no appetite in the morning and end up eating most of your food after dinner or at night, or is your eating pattern mainly limited to these discrete binge episodes?\n\nPatient: My eating is mainly limited to these discrete episodes, which happen about one to three times a week. I eat a normal dinner and feel comfortably full beforehand, so it's not a daily pattern of skipping meals or having no appetite in the morning. It's just those specific nights where I suddenly lose control and eat massive amounts of food.\n\nDoctor: Outside of these binge episodes, do you usually eat very little during the day and most of your calories after dinner or at night, with little appetite in the morning? Or is your eating pattern normal except for these occasional loss-of-control binges?\n\nPatient: My eating pattern during the day and at dinner is completely normal, and I don't restrict my food at all. I eat a regular supper and feel comfortably full, but then around nine in the evening, I wander back into the kitchen and start overeating. It is really just during those late-night episodes that I lose control.\n\nDoctor: Outside of these binge episodes, do you usually eat very little during the day and most of your food after dinner or at night, or is your eating pattern normal except for these episodes?\n\nPatient: My eating pattern is generally normal during the day, and I eat a regular dinner and feel comfortably full. The problem is what happens later in the evening, around nine, when I go back into the kitchen and start eating large amounts of food despite not being hungry at all.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever wake up from sleep during the night and eat with little or no memory of it afterward, or is all of the eating happening only while you are fully awake in the evening?\n\nPatient: I am always fully awake when this happens, typically in the evening before I go to bed, around nine o'clock. I remember everything clearly, and sitting there fully aware of what I just ate is exactly what makes me feel so heavy and ashamed afterward.\n\nDoctor: Outside of these evening binge episodes, do you usually eat very little during the day and most of your calories after dinner or at night, with little appetite in the morning? Or is your eating pattern normal except for these episodes?\n\nPatient: My daytime eating is completely normal, and I don't skip meals or lack an appetite in the morning. I eat a regular supper and feel comfortably full, but the trouble is that around nine in the evening I wander back into the kitchen. That's when I start eating large amounts of food, even though I'm not actually hungry at all.\n\nDoctor: Outside of these evening binge episodes, do you usually eat very little during the day and most of your calories after dinner or at night, or is your eating pattern normal except for these episodes?\n\nPatient: My daytime eating is completely normal, and I eat a regular dinner that leaves me feeling comfortably full. The issue is strictly limited to those episodes that happen later in the evening, usually starting around nine o'clock.\n\nDoctor: Outside of these evening episodes, do you usually eat very little during the day and then get most of your food after dinner or at night, with little appetite in the morning? Or is your daytime eating normal and the problem only these discrete binge episodes?\n\nPatient: My daytime eating is completely normal, and I don't starve myself or skip meals during the day. The problem is strictly those discrete, out-of-control episodes that happen late in the evening, after I've already had a normal supper and feel full.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel a strong urge to eat mostly after your evening meal or late at night every day, with little appetite in the morning, or is your daytime eating pattern completely normal except for these binge episodes?\n\nPatient: My daytime eating is completely normal, and I eat a regular supper that leaves me comfortably full. The strong urges and overeating only happen late at night, usually around nine o'clock, but not every single day. They typically occur one to three times a week, especially after emotionally draining days.\n\nDoctor: Do these late-night eating episodes happen most nights with a persistent pattern of eating a large portion of your calories after dinner, or are they only occasional binge episodes a few times per week?\n\nPatient: They are definitely more occasional, happening a few times a week rather than every single night. It is rare for a week to go by without at least one of those nights, and on harder or more stressful weeks, it can happen two or three times. I always feel so embarrassed when I let myself slip like that.\n\nDoctor: Outside of these binge episodes, do you usually eat very little during the day and then most of your food after dinner or at night, with little appetite in the morning, or is your daytime eating otherwise normal?\n\nPatient: My daytime eating is completely normal, and I don't starve myself during the day. I eat a regular supper and feel comfortably full afterward, so the late-night eating around nine PM happens despite having eaten normally earlier. It's not because I am restricting myself or skipping meals.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel that your self-worth is strongly tied to your weight or body shape, or that you are eating unusually large amounts of food in a short time with a clear sense of loss of control?\n\nPatient: I do feel terribly embarrassed about my appearance and how my clothes don't fit, and I'm filled with shame after I eat. During those episodes, I absolutely lose control; it is like a switch flips and I can't stop myself from polishing off huge amounts of food, like half a pan of lasagna and bowls of ice cream, in less than an hour.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever do anything to prevent weight gain after these episodes, such as vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively, or is it only the binge eating without any compensatory behavior?\n\nPatient: No, I never do any of those things like vomiting, fasting, or exercising excessively to prevent weight gain. Instead, I just sit in the quiet kitchen afterward feeling incredibly heavy, ashamed, and guilty, beating myself up mentally. I don't do anything to try to get rid of the food or reverse what I've done.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had periods where you intentionally ate much less during the day or skipped meals to make up for the night eating, or is your daytime eating always normal?"

No, my daytime eating is always normal, and I don't intentionally skip meals or restrict my food to make up for those nights. I don't do anything to try to reverse it.\n\nDoctor: Do you find that most of your food intake happens after dinner or at night, and do you ever wake up from sleep to eat with little or no memory of it afterward?\n\nPatient: Yes, these episodes almost always happen late in the evening after dinner, before I go to bed. However, I never wake up from my sleep to eat, and I don't have any memory loss about it. I am completely awake and vividly remember everything afterward, which is why I feel so much guilt and shame.\n\nDoctor: When you eat at night, are you fully awake and aware the whole time, or do you ever wake up from sleep and find that you ate with little or no memory of it afterward?\n\nPatient: Yes, I am completely awake and aware the entire time. It always happens in the evening before I go to bed, around nine o'clock, and never while I am asleep. I remember everything vividly, which is why I feel so much guilt and shame afterward while sitting in the kitchen looking at the empty dishes.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever wake up from sleep and eat with little or no memory of it afterward, or are these episodes always while you are fully awake and aware?\n\nPatient: No, I never wake up from sleep to eat, and I don't have any memory gaps. These episodes always happen when I am fully awake and aware, usually around nine in the evening before I've even gone to bed. Unfortunately, I remember every single detail, which just leaves me feeling deeply ashamed and full of regret afterward.\n\nDoctor: Do you usually eat most of your daily food after dinner or at night, with little appetite in the morning, or are the episodes mainly discrete binges that can happen at any time of day?\n\nPatient: These are discrete episodes that happen late in the evening, usually around nine o'clock, rather than continuous grazing. It only happens as those discrete episodes in the evening when I am fully awake, usually around nine o'clock or in the hour before I go to bed.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least 3 months where most of your daily food intake happened after your evening meal or after waking from sleep, with little or no appetite in the morning?\n\nPatient: While I do eat a large amount of food late in the evening before going to bed, I definitely don't wake up from sleep to eat. I also don't recall having a loss of appetite in the morning.\n\nDoctor: Do you usually have little or no appetite in the morning and end up eating most of your food after dinner or at night, or is your eating pattern mainly limited to these discrete binge episodes?\n\nPatient: My eating is mainly limited to these discrete episodes, which happen about one to three times a week.
